verified: The admin sidepanel's shared Site access control appeared on the actual page and exposed the temporary Chrome-toolbar path plus separate persistent grant and target-page reload actions.

The product persistent request opened Chrome's native origin-scoped permission sheet. Deny showed an explicit refusal while preserving the toolbar path; a later Allow succeeded and the product showed the granted state.
Prepare completed on Nuxt in 757 ms with three scroll steps under Chrome's temporary per-visit access path while its site setting remained Ask on every visit and before the persistent grant.

SEO rendered real, page-specific Nuxt and IANA results. Navigation while the control was open invalidated the prior page state; reopening Site access and reopening the sidepanel followed the new IANA origin. The separate Reload page action reloaded the browser target and IANA SEO data remained populated afterward.

In a second run with the sidepanel left open, changing Chrome to Ask on every visit and reloading the target without reopening Matrx from the toolbar reproduced Prepare remaining at Preparing… . The product Site access control opened Chrome's real origin-scoped permission sheet; after Allow, the product showed Access allowed. Its separate Reload page action cleared the old pending view, and a fresh Prepare succeeded in 756 ms with three scroll steps.
verdict_A_live_user_outcome.limits: Bounded admin-user acceptance of the named access/recovery flows only. The first run's toolbar open granted temporary per-visit access before Prepare, but the second run reproduced the pending state without reopening Matrx. The second run proves visible grant → explicit reload → successful fresh Prepare; it does not establish whether the original pending injection returns before reload or whether a late stale completion is ignored. The temporary Prepare success was not instrumented to read chrome.permissions.contains from product runtime; the linked earlier ephemeral-click probe supplies separate Chrome API evidence for contains(origin)=false compatibility. Unsupported API, non-HTTP(S), and guest/member behavior remain unverified.

verdict_B_evidence_quality.evidence: Runs site-access-native-acceptance-20261002-01 and site-access-native-recovery-20261002-02 used separate uniquely owned profiles privately cloned from the frozen173 admin profile. Both used the exact imported receipt artifact; independent tree hashing matched the receipt, and the loaded CFT extension ID plus authenticated admin product UI were visible. Native Chrome UI supplied the permission Deny/Allow sheet, site settings, and target reload observations. Both resource journals ended with valid terminal decisions.
verdict_B_evidence_quality.limits: Evidence supports only the named flows on the admin seat with Chrome for Testing 149 and imported artifact 0.2.175. It does not certify inaccessible/unreachable branches or guest/member accounts, and does not determine whether the first pending call returns before explicit reload.
